The trick is clear to me now: make full use of every form of neutralization, while at the same time taking control of the point from which the decisive command is given. For example: introduce Gottgläubigkeit, “belief in God,” as an official creed.

As ideological content, this is about as neutral and as empty of any real decision as anything that exists in Europe today. At bottom, it can even remain neutral and non-committal in relation to the choice between theism and atheism. After all, Christians, Jews, pantheists, deists—all of them, in one way or another, believe in God. But now comes the decisive occupation of that neutral point:
I decide what counts as belief in God.
A devout Jew suddenly no longer counts as a believer in God, even though he may be as God-believing as anyone one can imagine.
Are you a believer in God or not? And so on.

I have known the violent jerks of fate, Victories and defeats, revolutions and restorations, Inflations and deflations, being bombed out And being defamed, changes of regime and burst pipes, Hunger and cold, camps and solitary confinement. I have passed through all of it, And all of it has passed through me.

I know the many forms of terror, Terror from above and terror from below, Terror on land and terror from the air, Legal terror and terror outside the law, Brown terror, red terror, and mottled terror, And the worst terror of all, which no one dares to name. I know them all, and I know how they work.
I know the chanting choruses of power and law, The loudspeakers of regimes and their distorters of meaning, The blacklists filled with names And the card indexes of the persecutors.

What am I supposed to sing now? The hymn Placebo? Am I supposed to become free of problems and envy plants and animals? Tremble in panic among the little Pans? Share the happiness of the mosquito that jumps inward?

Surely the most important condition, cause, consequence, and effect of placing limits on land warfare was the restriction of the concept of the enemy.
An economic competitor is not an enemy even during war.
In naval warfare, by contrast, he is an enemy. And that means that even between two wars—in other words, during peace—he remains a potential enemy.
The condition of peace between two land wars is therefore something fundamentally different from the condition of peace between two naval wars.

What “line” lies behind the atomic bomb and the other bacteriological, biological, genocidal, and similar highly scientific, highly progressive, highly modern means of fighting a “just war” in the modern sense?
Not a Maginot Line, which still had something almost touchingly terrestrial about it.
Not a global line in the sense of the Raya, the Amity Line, or the line of the Western Hemisphere. Those still imagined the globe in terms of its surface.
Instead, a space. And before that space can be filled with the proper content—cuius economia, eius regio—it must first be emptied completely and turned into a tabula rasa.
